# PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES] Contents of this Part

## General

## 64.1

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (1) This Part contains rules –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (a) in Section I, about claims relating to –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (i) the administration of estates of deceased persons, and

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (ii) trusts; and

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (b) in Section II, about charity proceedings.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (2) In this Part and Practice Directions 64A and 64B, where appropriate, references to trustees include executors and administrators.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.1] (3) All proceedings in the High Court to which this Part applies must be brought in the Chancery Division.

## I CLAIMS RELATING TO THE ADMINISTRATION OF ESTATES AND TRUSTS

## Scope of this Section

## 64.2

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] This Section of this Part applies to claims –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (a) for the court to determine any question arising in –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (i) the administration of the estate of a deceased person; or

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (ii) the execution of a trust;

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (b) for an order for the administration of the estate of a deceased person, or the execution of a trust, to be carried out under the direction of the court (‘an administration order’);

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (c) under the Variation of Trusts Act 1958 1 ; or

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.2] (d) under section 48 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 2 .

## Claim form

## 64.3

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.3] A claim to which this Section applies must be made by issuing a Part 8 claim form.

## Parties

## 64.4

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (1) In a claim to which this Section applies, other than an application under section 48 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (a) all the trustees must be parties;

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (b) if the claim is made by trustees, any of them who does not consent to being a claimant must be made a defendant; and

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (c) the claimant may make parties to the claim any persons with an interest in or claim against the estate, or an interest under the trust, who it is appropriate to make parties having regard to the nature of the order sought.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (2) In addition, in a claim under the Variation of Trusts Act 1958, unless the court directs otherwise any person who –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (a) created the trust; or

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (b) provided property for the purposes of the trust,

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] must, if still alive, be made a party to the claim.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.4] (The court may, under rule 19.2, order additional persons to be made parties to a claim.)

## II CHARITY PROCEEDINGS

## Scope of this Section and interpretation

## 64.5

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.5] (1) This Section applies to charity proceedings.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.5] (2) In this Section –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.5] (a) ‘the Act’ means the Charities Act 1993 3 ;

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.5] (b) ‘charity proceedings’ has the same meaning as in section 33(8) of the Act; and

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.5] (c) ‘the Commissioners’ means the Charity Commissioners for England and Wales.

## Application for permission to take charity proceedings

## 64.6

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (1) An application to the High Court under section 33(5) of the Act for permission to start charity proceedings must be made within 21 days after the refusal by the Commissioners of an order authorising proceedings.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (2) The application must be made by issuing a Part 8 claim form, which must contain the information specified in Practice Direction 64A.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (3) The Commissioners must be made defendants to the claim, but the claim form need not be served on them or on any other person.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (4) The judge considering the application may direct the Commissioners to file a written statement of their reasons for their decision.

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (5) The court will serve on the applicant a copy of any statement filed under paragraph (4).

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (6) The judge may either –

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (a) give permission without a hearing; or

[PART 64 – ESTATES, TRUSTS AND CHARITIES > 64.6] (b) fix a hearing.

## Footnotes

## 1. 1958 c.53.

## 2. 1985 c.61. Section 48 has been amended by the Courts and Legal Services Act 1990 (c.41).

## 3. 1993 c.10.
